reason: Compared the full source def:interlace and its inherited Gauss-visit conventions with SM.interlacement_definition and every concrete definition giving that aggregate meaning. The preceding source Gauss-visit construction is on a generic polygon, and the aggregate retains that domain with only n>=3, the actual tuple P and Generic P. Crossing P is the previously verified type of actual unordered remote edge pairs with nonempty geometric intersection. Each crossing has exactly two edge visits, whose traversal positions use the actual unique intersection parameters on the half-open traversal circle. crossing_visits_exist and crossing_visits_exhaust prove that any two different members exhaust the visit fibre; no arbitrary pair of external positions is supplied. Interlaces requires distinct crossings and witnesses consisting of those two actual visits of each crossing. Its two opposite-open-arc conditions express exactly the cyclic order x0,y0,x1,y1 up to rotation, with the source orientation and strict endpoint exclusion. traversalBetween is the already verified numerical-cut circular order, not an unbounded linear betweenness predicate. The complementary-arc proof checks all required position inequalities: distinct crossings have distinct traversal visits by Generic, and the two visits of one crossing are distinct. Thus it does not treat a shared endpoint as belonging to the complementary open arc or assume the desired exactly-one property. interlaces_iff_count proves the source equivalent formulation for every fixed distinct pair of x visits, not merely a conveniently chosen ordering. The cardinality counts the actual two visits of y; swapping x's visit order gives the same exactly-one condition. Symmetry is proved by rotating the four actual positions, and irreflexivity is explicit. interlacementGraph is a genuine SimpleGraph with vertex type exactly Crossing P and adjacency exactly this geometric Interlaces predicate. It is not an arbitrary input graph or a weakened graph with only some crossings or edges. independentSupports filters the entire powerset of the finite crossing universe by the actual graph IsIndepSet predicate, and membership equivalence plus explicit empty membership cover every independent subset including the empty set. Finsets lose no source subset because the actual crossing type is finite on the source domain. supportNeighbors and supportUnselected accept every support S, without an independence hypothesis. N(S) consists precisely of all crossing vertices interlacing some member of S; it does not delete S, so an element of S adjacent to another element of S is correctly retained. U(S) is exactly the full crossing universe minus S union N(S), with the aggregate's membership equivalence accounting for both exclusions. Relabelling is also proved on the actual constructions: the two-edge fibre equivalences transport every visit, arbitrary-point cyclic order preservation transports its open arcs, and interlaces_shift is an iff under crossingShiftEquiv. The supplied graph isomorphism uses exactly that vertex equivalence. The aggregate then proves independence-membership equivalence and exact N/U image equalities under the induced finite-support map for arbitrary S. No external ordering, graph, neighbourhood oracle, disjoint-neighbourhood assumption or desired-invariance premise has been added. Empty crossing universes and empty supports remain allowed. The semantic dependency inventory binds the inherited geometric crossing/visit meanings as well as Interlaces, the graph and all three support constructions. The source file and all 19 inspected local supporting files match the current passed checkpoint-015 receipt; previously reviewed shared dependencies are unchanged. The receipt audits 532 declarations with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound and explicitly does not accept the overall stage. countersignature_20260913.reason: The printed def:interlace (reference/SM/sm-1-polygons.tex:259-268, byte-identical extract in blueprint/STATEMENTS_AND_PROOFS.md:315-330; not reworded in SM15) defines, for a generic P, (1) interlacing of two distinct crossings x,y in X(P) as the four visits occurring in cyclic order x0<y0<x1<y1 up to rotation, equivalently exactly one visit of y between the two visits of x; (2) the interlacement graph G_P on vertex set X(P); (3) Ind(G_P) including the empty set; (4) N(S) and U(S)=X(P)\(S∪N(S)) for arbitrary S⊆X(P). The Lean definitions denote these objects. Domain: work/lean/SM/InterlaceDefinition.lean:13 takes 3≤n, a labelled tuple P and Generic P (Generic.lean:11-19 is exactly (G1),(G2)); working on labelled tuples is licensed by the source's formalization remark (sm-1-polygons.tex:55-61) and the shift clauses record equivariance. X(P): Crossings.lean:12-15 is the unordered pair {i,j} of remote edge indices (Polygon.lean:63-66 matches 'adjacent iff j-i in {-1,0,1}') with E_i∩E_j nonempty (edgeSegment Polygon.lean:54-55 = [mu_i, mu_{i+1}]). Visits: GaussVisits.lean:17 gives each crossing its two edge-labelled visits, and visitPosition (GaussVisits.lean:48-52) is (i, t_{ij}) with t the unique parameter of the crossing point on E_i (Crossings.lean:41-78), i.e. the source's visit on Gamma(P). Traversal circle and cyclic order: TraversalPoint = ZMod n × Ico 0 1 (Traversal.lean:12) and traversalBetween (Traversal.lean:73-76) is strict cyclic betweenness derived from the lexicographic key i.val+t, which is exactly the source's order '(i,t)<(i,t') for t<t' and (i,t)<(i+1,t')' read cyclically (the cut at label 0 is immaterial for the ternary relation). Interlacement: Interlacement.lean:16-20 requires x≠y and the existence of the two distinct visits x0,x1 of x and y0,y1 of y with y0 on the open arc x0→x1 and y1 on the open arc x1→x0, which is the cyclic order x0<y0<x1<y1 up to rotation; clause 2 of the aggregate (lines 19-21, via crossingVisitsOnArc InterlaceCount.lean:48-52) states the 'exactly one visit of y between the two visits of x' formulation for every choice of the two x visits, so both arc readings are covered. Graph: InterlaceSupports.lean:14-17 is a SimpleGraph on Crossing P with Adj = Interlaces. Ind(G_P): InterlaceSupports.lean:27-30 filters the full powerset of the finite crossing type by IsIndepSet, and the aggregate asserts the empty support is included (line 27). N(S), U(S): InterlaceSupports.lean:49-52 and 60-63 are {y | ∃x∈S, y interlaces x} and univ \ (S ∪ N(S)) for arbitrary S, as printed. Nothing is vacuous: Crossing P, Generic and the visit positions are the concrete geometric notions with no extra hypotheses.
